Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: E-value fusion: dependence-robust, betting-based per-image anomaly evidence from support normals
SUMMARY: Convert each level/branch patch score into an e-value (a likelihood-ratio-like betting score calibrated on the support normals), average e-values across levels and branches — valid under any dependence — and decide by the e-value's guarantee P(E >= 1/alpha) <= alpha.
HYPOTHESIS: E-value fusion yields realised false-positive rates at or below nominal (5%) on held-out BMAD modalities for K >= 4 while losing at most 1.5 image AUROC points relative to harmonic-mean p-value fusion.
RATIONALE: Harmonic-mean p-values remain only approximately valid and can be anti-conservative at very small levels. A different, exact route borrowed from game-theoretic statistics is to use e-values: the arithmetic mean of e-values is again an e-value under arbitrary dependence, so MVFA's correlated levels and branches can be combined exactly, and Markov's inequality gives a guaranteed false-positive bound. Calibrating p-values from the support normals into e-values (via a calibrator such as kappa p^(kappa - 1)) needs no labels.
METHOD: 1) Per patch, branch and level, empirical p from support LOO nulls. 2) E-value calibrator e = kappa p^(kappa - 1) with kappa = 0.5 (ablation 0.25, 0.75). 3) Per-patch fused e-value = mean over the 8 terms; image e-value = mean of top-2% patch e-values (an average of e-values remains an e-value under the null); decision at E >= 1/alpha. 4) Code: scoring.py evalue_fusion().
EXPERIMENT: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: harmonic-mean fusion; Brown-corrected Fisher; Fisher. Metrics: realised FPR at alpha in {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}, sensitivity, image AUROC. Falsification: AUROC loss above 3 points.

Idea B:
TITLE: FDR-controlled anomaly maps: Benjamini-Yekutieli discoveries per image from support-anchored pixel p-values
SUMMARY: Treat every patch of a test image as a hypothesis test against the support normals, apply the Benjamini-Yekutieli procedure (valid under dependence) at a target false discovery rate, and score the image by the mass of discovered patches.
HYPOTHESIS: At q = 0.1, the proportion of discovered patches that fall outside true lesions on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC images stays at or below 0.15, and the image score 'discovered mass' achieves image AUROC within 1 point of harmonic-mean fusion with region pooling.
RATIONALE: The parent controls error at the image level, but its pixel threshold for regions (99th percentile of support maps) has no statistical meaning. By analogy with voxel-wise inference in neuroimaging, a per-image anomaly map is a multiple-testing problem: hundreds of correlated patch tests, of which a few may be true anomalies. FDR control gives the map itself a guarantee (expected fraction of false patches among flagged ones), which is the clinically relevant quantity for localisation, and the Benjamini-Yekutieli variant holds under arbitrary dependence between neighbouring patches.
METHOD: 1) Per patch, combined p-value across levels and branches with the harmonic mean (support LOO nulls). 2) Per image, Benjamini-Yekutieli at q in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} over the 289 patches. 3) Image score = number of discoveries (or summed -log p over discoveries); image threshold from support LOO images. 4) Pixel map for evaluation = discoveries upsampled, plus the continuous -log p map for AUROC. 5) Code: scoring.py by_fdr().
EXPERIMENT: BMAD leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); MVFA checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits and the MVFA baseline re-run the same way; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: harmonic-mean + region mass; Fisher + top-2%; transductive MVFA. Metrics: realised false discovery proportion of flagged patches (masked datasets), sensitivity per lesion, image AUROC, pixel AUROC, PRO. Falsification: realised FDP above 2q on average.

WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
